title: "Biography"
subtitle: "From a Vermont bedroom to Stick Season"
---

## Early Life

Noah Kahan was born in 1997 and raised in Strafford, Vermont, a small rural town he has described as
central to both his identity and his songwriting. Music was part of his household growing up, and he began
writing songs and posting them online as a teenager, building a following on platforms like YouTube and
SoundCloud before he had a record deal.

## Getting Discovered

Kahan's early single "Young Blood" caught the attention of Republic Records, leading to a record deal while
he was still a teenager. He spent his late teens and early twenties developing his sound, releasing music
that leaned closer to conventional pop before returning to the folk and acoustic influences of his
childhood.

## Breaking Through

::: {.callout-quote}
"Stick season, it's already got its icy grip on me" — the opening line that launched a thousand playlists.
:::

His 2021 EP *Cape Elizabeth* signaled a turn toward the introspective, New England-rooted sound that would
define his career. That shift crystallized with the 2022 release of his third studio album, **Stick
Season**, named for the bleak stretch of late autumn in northern New England after the leaves have fallen
and before the snow arrives. The album — and its title track in particular — went viral on TikTok and
streaming platforms, resonating with listeners far outside Vermont who connected with its themes of
homesickness, arrested development, and small-town restlessness.

## The Stick Season Era

Kahan followed the album with deluxe reissues (*Stick Season (We'll All Be Here Forever)* and *Stick Season
(Forever)*), packed with additional tracks and high-profile collaborations, including "Northern Attitude"
with Zach Bryan and "Call Your Mom" with Lizzy McAlpine. The extended rollout kept the project in the
cultural conversation for nearly two years, moving him from small clubs to headlining arenas and festivals
worldwide.
